summary: This comparative analysis surveys national education initiatives launched since the academic year began on September 1, 2023, to build global citizenship and multicultural awareness. It covers programs in Scandinavia, Africa, Asia, the Americas, the Middle East and Europe, each with its own emphasis, such as languages, indigenous culture, technology, leadership, peace-building or project-based learning. Together they form a mosaic of strategies for producing globally aware, culturally competent citizens.
one_line: A survey of national programs in 2023-2024 across many regions that teach global citizenship and multicultural awareness in schools.
key_facts: Sweden's Ministry of Education, led by Minister Per Larsson, launched the "Världsklass" (World Class) initiative in October 2023, giving every student from sixth grade up the chance to learn at least two foreign languages and join an exchange program before graduating.

Finland's "Global Suomi" (Global Finland), unveiled by Minister of Education Liisa Virtanen in November 2023, focuses on a bespoke global citizenship curriculum and experiential learning, including international culture days and interaction with embassies and cultural institutes.

Kenya's "Nyota ya Afrika" (Star of Africa) program, spearheaded by Education Secretary Dr. James Mwangi and introduced in January 2024, teaches African cultural heritages and partners with schools on other continents via modern communication technologies.
South Africa's "Ubuntu Connect" was rolled out in March 2024 under Education Minister Naledi Mokoena and sets up "sister school" relationships with institutions in Asia and South America.
Japan's "Kokoro Project," instigated in February 2024 by Minister of Education Hiroshi Tanaka, uses VR technology for virtual exchanges so students can 'visit' classrooms around the world.
Singapore's "One World, Many Stories" campaign, announced in mid-2023 by Minister of Education Lim Chee Hoon, weaves narratives of various cultures into subjects from literature to social studies.

The United States' "Citizens Without Borders" program, led by Education Secretary Maria Gonzalez and launched in Fall 2023, integrates global education benchmarks into curricula at all grade levels and offers international service-learning projects on issues like climate change and social justice.

Canada's "Global Leaders of Tomorrow" initiative, introduced in October 2023 by Minister of Education Thomas Jackson, provides mentorship from industry and political leaders and cross-cultural competence training.

The United Arab Emirates launched "Al-Mawtini Al-Aalami" (The Global Citizen) in late 2023 under Education Chief Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, celebrating local culture while embracing the country's cosmopolitan makeup.

Israel's "Peaceful Horizons" program, unveiled in September 2023 and administered by Director of Education Sarah Cohen, teaches geopolitics within a framework of conflict resolution and peace-building.

France's "Citoyen du Monde" (Citizens of the World), led by Education Minister Jean Lefevre and begun in September 2023, teaches global geography, international relations and multiculturalism from primary school onwards.

Germany's "Weltbürger Werden" (Becoming World Citizens), rolled out by Minister of Education Katarina Baumgartner in December 2023, uses project-based learning on cross-border issues such as the European Union's political mechanisms and the experiences of refugees and immigrants.
